business_model: Hardware sale (stationary bike) plus recurring subscription for streamed classes
anti_contamination_note: Cutoff frozen at 2016-06-18 (the Fortune article's publish date, the latest dated primary source located for this snapshot window) before evidence beyond 'Peloton exists, mid-2016' was gathered.

historical_evidence.company: Founded 2012, launched publicly in early 2014, a connected-fitness hardware company selling an internet-connected stationary bike with live and on-demand streamed classes.
historical_evidence.market: Home-fitness/connected-hardware market; the article frames the company as building a new category (premium connected fitness hardware) rather than competing directly in an established one.
historical_evidence.team: No specific founder-background detail found in the primary source reviewed for this snapshot.
historical_evidence.product: Hardware (bike) plus software (streamed classes) bundle; priced at $1,995 per bike plus a $39/month subscription for class content.
historical_evidence.execution: By the snapshot date had raised $120 million total (Catterton, Tiger Global, True Ventures) across rounds including an April 2015 Series C ($30M) and a subsequent round; had expanded to 50 U.S. retail locations.
historical_evidence.traction: Disclosed close to 40,000 bikes sold since the early-2014 launch, as of the June 2016 snapshot -- a real, dated, primary-sourced unit-sales figure. Prior comparison point: an April 2015 Series C announcement (a separate primary source) disclosed more than 10,000 bikes sold across all 50 states and 16 countries as of that earlier date.
historical_evidence.financial: Historical revenue of approximately $80 million in sales over 2014-2015 combined (hardware only, excluding subscription revenue) was disclosed, alongside a stated five-fold revenue increase in 2015 versus 2014, and a company-stated 2016 revenue projection of $150 million. The company claimed profitability but 'didn't reveal any further financial details' -- a real, dated, but self-reported and unquantified positive claim, treated accordingly (see Unit Economics rationale below).

normalized_facts.note: hardware sales only, explicitly excluding subscription revenue
